title: Baked rhubarb and clementines with almond crumble

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Fruit, nuts, sugar, spices and rapeseed oil are all plain cupboard foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Forced rhubarb, clementines, ground almonds and hazelnuts are all everyday Tesco lines in late February.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, a board, a bowl and a baking dish, and the method is simple tossing and scattering.

works.reason: 400g of rhubarb with six clementines and a 150g nut topping is a sensible snack for four, and 25 to 30 minutes at 190°C will soften the rhubarb and colour the crumble.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes covers cutting the rhubarb, peeling, slicing and juicing the clementines and chopping the hazelnuts, and the 30-minute bake matches the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and both spices appear in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm baked fruit crumble suits a cold late-February afternoon, and the clementines are a main part of the fruit rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is mostly fruit and nuts with only modest added sugar, a satisfying real-food snack a family would make again.
